You are an experienced NSW HSC Modern History marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2019 NSW HSC Modern History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting. Judge the response the way HSC Modern History markers do: a direct answer to the question, a sustained judgement where the directive verb asks for one, specific and accurate evidence (dates, names, cases, legislation, sources, historians) and the terms of the course. Do not reward length or narrative for its own sake.

Question 15 (b) [25 marks]: How significant were the Allied strategies to their victory in Europe?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 25):
21–25 marks: Addresses the question asked providing a clear explanation OR judgement based on a sophisticated and sustained argument which demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of the issue(s) raised in the question | Supports the argument with extensive and accurate historical knowledge and understanding including relevant evidence and interpretation | Presents a well-structured, logical and cohesive response using appropriate historical terms and concepts
16–20 marks: Addresses the question asked providing an explanation OR judgement based on a coherent argument which demonstrates a sound understanding of the issue(s) raised in the question | Provides detailed and accurate historical knowledge and understanding including relevant evidence and interpretation | Presents a well-structured response using appropriate historical terms and concepts
11–15 marks: Addresses the question asked with a relevant but largely narrative or descriptive response which may contain an implied understanding of the issue(s) raised in the question | Provides relevant and accurate historical knowledge and understanding | Presents a structured response using some appropriate historical terms and concepts
6–10 marks: Presents a generalised, mostly relevant narrative or descriptive response | Provides some historical knowledge and understanding | Communicates using some appropriate historical terms and/or concepts
1–5 marks: Makes general statement(s) in relation to the question | May use some historical terms and/or concepts


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Possible thesis: While Allied strategies were important to their victory in war in Europe it was German failures throughout the war which determined the outcome of the war.
Supporting evidence COULD include:
Allied strategies such as:
• Allied strategic bombing of Germany throughout the war and its impact on German resources, production and morale
• Operation Bagration and the Russian counterattacks on the Eastern Front (strength and organisation)
• D-Day and the Western Fronts 1944–1945 – coordinated attacks under coordinated Allied command
• Coordination of timing between Eastern & Western Fronts in 1944–1945 (various Allied powers working together).
Other reasons for the Allied victory could include:
• Failure of Axis strategies (in the air, in Africa, on the Eastern Front)
• Extent of occupied territories and diversion of manpower needed to control them
• German loss of allies (especially Italy but also failures by Japan in the Pacific)
• The significance of the US coming to Europe to aid the Allies from D-Day onwards (both militarily and in terms of morale)
• German homefront challenges:
– Late decision to go to Total war
– Impacts of bombing
– Distraction of the Holocaust
• Allied homefront successes – especially the British.



STUDENT RESPONSE:

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-25>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '21–25'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a 6 to 8 line plan of what a full-mark response would cover, one line per paragraph, not a full essay>"}
